The Osun State Police Command has warned residents against engaging in jungle justice, urging them to instead allow the appropriate authorities to investigate and handle reported offences in accordance with the law. The command made the warning known in a statement signed by its spokesperson, Abiodun Ojelabi, on Thursday. Ojelabi said the warning was in reaction to the killing of a man who was said to be travelling in a vehicle that was allegedly involved in an accident that killed two pedestrians in Ilesa, Osun State. The PPRO said the deceased and others were in the vehicle that allegedly hit and killed two pedestrians identified as Silas Seun and Matthew Dada. Ojelabi further said, “Osun State Police Command wishes to inform the public that on 18th November 2026, the Command received information about a fatal road traffic accident involving an unregistered Toyota Camry, a TVS motorcycle and two pedestrians, identified as Silas Seun (female) and Matthew Dada (male). Make PUNCH part of your everyday experience. Add us to your Preferred Sources “The unfortunate incident resulted in the immediate death of the two pedestrians at the scene of the accident. The driver of the vehicle, one Favour Fabunmi, ‘M’, 23 years old, and the other occupants of the Toyota Camry were successfully rescued alive. “However, in a disturbing turn of events, one of the rescued occupants was attacked and severely beaten by an angry mob. “He was subsequently rushed to the hospital but was later confirmed dead. The vehicle was also set ablaze by the mob and completely burnt to ashes.” Mob kills accident survivor after crash claims two lives in Osun ASUP begins strike in four South-West states over unpaid allowances Tinubu, South-West govs invited to Adeleke’s second-term inauguration Reacting further to the development, Ojelabi said the matter had been transferred to the command headquarters for a comprehensive investigation, adding that necessary legal procedures had also been initiated. He also said the state Commissioner of Police, Ibrahim Zungura, “strongly condemns the act of mob violence and warns members of the public against taking the law into their hands. “Members of the public are therefore urged to resist the temptation to administer instant justice, irrespective of the circumstances, and allow the appropriate authorities to investigate and handle reported offences in accordance with the law.” He said the CP assured the public that the command would leave no stone unturned “in identifying all individuals who participated in the mob action, and anyone found culpable would be arrested and prosecuted in accordance with the law.” He urged members of the public to remain calm, law-abiding and security-conscious, encouraging citizens to promptly report accidents and criminal incidents to the nearest police station rather than resorting to violence. PUNCH Metro earlier reported that the command said it had commenced an investigation into the killing of Monica Mary, a student of Westland University, Iwo, who was allegedly stabbed to death by some unknown assailants.
